Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.
# This repo's validation CI is `Quality` (display name "Quality") and its
# required context is the `crap` job.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # dmtools-agents#682 (live fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03, still reproducing
  # 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22 in THIS repo — runs 06:36/06:41/06:43): the
  # global group below already ran with cancel-in-progress:false, yet
  # kicker runs kept dying cancelled in chains. cancel-in-progress only
  # shields the RUNNING run — a queued run in the same group ALWAYS
  # supersedes (cancels) the pending one (GitHub docs: "Any existing
  # pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists,
  # will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its
  # place"). One global group meant every push anywhere (silent refresh,
  # factory-data snapshots, dev waves) cancelled every other branch's
  # pending kicker. Per-head-SHA group: no push can displace another
  # push's kicker — a queued kicker that is about to dispatch a tick
  # always gets to run (canonical fix + consumer notes: IstiN/
  # dmtools-agentic-workflows factory-sm-kicker.yml). Effective once the
  # canonical pin is bumped (separate PR): until then the called
  # workflow's own global group still supersedes.
  group: sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: crap

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Regenerate the factory board visual-check fixtures (site/factory/visual-check/).
#
# The board is zero-build and reads live `factory-data` snapshots; these
# fixtures are captured against the BUNDLED fixture snapshot instead
# (visual-check/fixture.json, via the board's ?fixture= mode) so every
# surface — lane summaries, progress bars, backlog lanes, details drawer,
# token table — renders deterministically, no network, no rate limits.
#
# Requires a headless-capable chromium on PATH. The board pins "now" to the
# fixture's tick time in fixture mode, so re-runs produce identical frames.
#
# Usage: bash site/factory/visual-check/capture.sh
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."   # site/factory — the board root (fixture URLs are relative to it)

CHROME="${CHROME:-$(command -v chromium || command -v chromium-browser || command -v google-chrome)}"
BASE="file://$PWD/index.html"
OUT="visual-check"
FIXTURE="visual-check/fixture.json"

shot() { # shot <name> <w> <h> <query>
  local name="$1" w="$2" h="$3" q="$4"
  "$CHROME" --headless=new --no-sandbox --disable-gpu \
    --allow-file-access-from-files --hide-scrollbars \
    --window-size="$w,$h" --virtual-time-budget=5000 \
    --screenshot="$OUT/$name" "$BASE?$q" 2>/dev/null
  echo "  $name"
}

echo "capturing factory-board visual-check fixtures (fixture=$FIXTURE)"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.1440x900.dark.png"          1440 900  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.1440x900.light.png"         1440 900  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=light"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.2048x1320.dark.png"         2048 1320 "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.390x844.dark.mobile.png"    390  844  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark"
# the drawer is an overlay — captured open (deep-linked) as its own frame
shot "factory-board.visual-check.1440x900.dark.drawer.png"   1440 900  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark&drawer=pr-817@validating"
echo "done"

{"command":"node -e \"const f=require('./site/factory/visual-check/fixture.json'); for (const [k,v] of Object.entries(f.lanes)) { for (const c of (Array.isArray(v)?v:[])) { if (c.title) console.log(k, c.pr, c.title.length + ' chars'); } }\""}
{"command":"grep -rn \"860\" site/factory/visual-check/fixture.json | head -5; grep -n \"drawer=pr-\" site/factory/visual-check/capture.sh"}

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-06):

The visual check is the only automated safety net for this CSS, but every title in `visual-check/fixture.json` is ≤ 51 chars — at the ~156px title content width that is at most 3 rendered lines, i.e. exactly at (never past) the `-webkit-line-clamp: 3` limit. **ai-teammate** (2026-10-06):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `.lbl` ellipsis is now unreachable; `white-space: normal` is redundant**

Two small polish notes on the same mechanism:

With `overflow-wrap: anywhere` added here, a long label now always wraps mid-token instead of overflowing, so `text-overflow: ellipsis` on `.lbl` can never trigger anymore — content always fits by wrapping. `-webkit-line-clamp` only clips content when the element also has `overflow: hidden` (this PR removes the `overflow: hidden` that the old one-line ellipsis rule had).   /* multi-line, not a one-line ellipsis: long issue titles must wrap

  white-space: normal;
  display: -webkit-box; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; -webkit-line-clamp: 3;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
  overflow: hidden;              /* required for -webkit-line-clamp to clip */
}

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.
# This repo's validation CI is `Quality` (display name "Quality") and its
# required context is the `crap` job.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # dmtools-agents#682 (live fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03, still reproducing
  # 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22 in THIS repo — runs 06:36/06:41/06:43): the
  # global group below already ran with cancel-in-progress:false, yet
  # kicker runs kept dying cancelled in chains. cancel-in-progress only
  # shields the RUNNING run — a queued run in the same group ALWAYS
  # supersedes (cancels) the pending one (GitHub docs: "Any existing
  # pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists,
  # will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its
  # place"). One global group meant every push anywhere (silent refresh,
  # factory-data snapshots, dev waves) cancelled every other branch's
  # pending kicker. Per-head-SHA group: no push can displace another
  # push's kicker — a queued kicker that is about to dispatch a tick
  # always gets to run (canonical fix + consumer notes: IstiN/
  # dmtools-agentic-workflows factory-sm-kicker.yml). Effective once the
  # canonical pin is bumped (separate PR): until then the called
  # workflow's own global group still supersedes.
  group: sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: crap

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Regenerate the factory board visual-check fixtures (site/factory/visual-check/).
#
# The board is zero-build and reads live `factory-data` snapshots; these
# fixtures are captured against the BUNDLED fixture snapshot instead
# (visual-check/fixture.json, via the board's ?fixture= mode) so every
# surface — lane summaries, progress bars, backlog lanes, details drawer,
# token table — renders deterministically, no network, no rate limits.
#
# Requires a headless-capable chromium on PATH. The board pins "now" to the
# fixture's tick time in fixture mode, so re-runs produce identical frames.
#
# Usage: bash site/factory/visual-check/capture.sh
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."   # site/factory — the board root (fixture URLs are relative to it)

CHROME="${CHROME:-$(command -v chromium || command -v chromium-browser || command -v google-chrome)}"
BASE="file://$PWD/index.html"
OUT="visual-check"
FIXTURE="visual-check/fixture.json"

shot() { # shot <name> <w> <h> <query>
  local name="$1" w="$2" h="$3" q="$4"
  "$CHROME" --headless=new --no-sandbox --disable-gpu \
    --allow-file-access-from-files --hide-scrollbars \
    --window-size="$w,$h" --virtual-time-budget=5000 \
    --screenshot="$OUT/$name" "$BASE?$q" 2>/dev/null
  echo "  $name"
}

echo "capturing factory-board visual-check fixtures (fixture=$FIXTURE)"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.1440x900.dark.png"          1440 900  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.1440x900.light.png"         1440 900  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=light"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.2048x1320.dark.png"         2048 1320 "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.390x844.dark.mobile.png"    390  844  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark"
# the drawer is an overlay — captured open (deep-linked) as its own frame
shot "factory-board.visual-check.1440x900.dark.drawer.png"   1440 900  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark&drawer=pr-817@validating"
echo "done"

{"command":"node -e \"const f=require('./site/factory/visual-check/fixture.json'); for (const [k,v] of Object.entries(f.lanes)) { for (const c of (Array.isArray(v)?v:[])) { if (c.title) console.log(k, c.pr, c.title.length + ' chars'); } }\""}

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

🚨 **BLOCKING: `-webkit-line-clamp` without `overflow: hidden` does not clip — titles longer than 3 lines bleed over the rows below the title**

`-webkit-line-clamp` only clips content when the element also has `overflow: hidden` (this PR removes the `overflow: hidden` that the old one-line ellipsis rule had). .title {

  /* multi-line, not a one-line ellipsis: long issue titles must wrap

  white-space: normal;
  display: -webkit-box; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; -webkit-line-clamp: 3;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
  overflow: hidden;              /* required for -webkit-line-clamp to clip */
}
```

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.
# This repo's validation CI is `Quality` (display name "Quality") and its
# required context is the `crap` job.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # dmtools-agents#682 (live fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03, still reproducing
  # 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22 in THIS repo — runs 06:36/06:41/06:43): the
  # global group below already ran with cancel-in-progress:false, yet
  # kicker runs kept dying cancelled in chains. cancel-in-progress only
  # shields the RUNNING run — a queued run in the same group ALWAYS
  # supersedes (cancels) the pending one (GitHub docs: "Any existing
  # pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists,
  # will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its
  # place"). One global group meant every push anywhere (silent refresh,
  # factory-data snapshots, dev waves) cancelled every other branch's
  # pending kicker. Per-head-SHA group: no push can displace another
  # push's kicker — a queued kicker that is about to dispatch a tick
  # always gets to run (canonical fix + consumer notes: IstiN/
  # dmtools-agentic-workflows factory-sm-kicker.yml). Effective once the
  # canonical pin is bumped (separate PR): until then the called
  # workflow's own global group still supersedes.
  group: sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: crap

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Regenerate the factory board visual-check fixtures (site/factory/visual-check/).
#
# The board is zero-build and reads live `factory-data` snapshots; these
# fixtures are captured against the BUNDLED fixture snapshot instead
# (visual-check/fixture.json, via the board's ?fixture= mode) so every
# surface — lane summaries, progress bars, backlog lanes, details drawer,
# token table — renders deterministically, no network, no rate limits.
#
# Requires a headless-capable chromium on PATH. The board pins "now" to the
# fixture's tick time in fixture mode, so re-runs produce identical frames.
#
# Usage: bash site/factory/visual-check/capture.sh
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."   # site/factory — the board root (fixture URLs are relative to it)

CHROME="${CHROME:-$(command -v chromium || command -v chromium-browser || command -v google-chrome)}"
BASE="file://$PWD/index.html"
OUT="visual-check"
FIXTURE="visual-check/fixture.json"

shot() { # shot <name> <w> <h> <query>
  local name="$1" w="$2" h="$3" q="$4"
  "$CHROME" --headless=new --no-sandbox --disable-gpu \
    --allow-file-access-from-files --hide-scrollbars \
    --window-size="$w,$h" --virtual-time-budget=5000 \
    --screenshot="$OUT/$name" "$BASE?$q" 2>/dev/null
  echo "  $name"
}

echo "capturing factory-board visual-check fixtures (fixture=$FIXTURE)"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.1440x900.dark.png"          1440 900  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.1440x900.light.png"         1440 900  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=light"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.2048x1320.dark.png"         2048 1320 "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.390x844.dark.mobile.png"    390  844  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark"
# the drawer is an overlay — captured open (deep-linked) as its own frame
shot "factory-board.visual-check.1440x900.dark.drawer.png"   1440 900  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark&drawer=pr-817@validating"
echo "done"

{"command":"node -e \"const f=require('./site/factory/visual-check/fixture.json'); for (const [k,v] of Object.entries(f.lanes)) { for (const c of (Array.isArray(v)?v:[])) { if (c.title) console.log(k, c.pr, c.title.length + ' chars'); } }\""}
{"command":"grep -rn \"860\" site/factory/visual-check/fixture.json | head -5; grep -n \"drawer=pr-\" site/factory/visual-check/capture.sh"}

      "body": "🚨 **BLOCKING: `-webkit-line-clamp` without `overflow: hidden` does not clip — titles longer than 3 lines bleed over the rows below the title**

`-webkit-line-clamp` only clips content when the element also has `overflow: hidden` (this PR removes the `overflow: hidden` that the old one-line ellipsis rule had). Without it, the box is clamped to 3 lines and an ellipsis is painted after line 3, **but lines 4+ are still painted below the box** (documented on MDN: *"otherwise the content is not clipped, although an ellipsis is still shown"*). On the card that overflow ink lands on the `.labels` / `.meta` / stepper rows.

Verified empirically on this exact board (headless Chromium, `?fixture=` mode, one card patched with a 185-char title — this repo's own PR titles reach that length):

- as shipped (no `overflow: hidden`): **1650** text pixels rendered in the card region below the clamped title box, overlapping the badge/meta/stepper rows, plus a misleading `…` after line 3;
- with `overflow: hidden` added: **210** pixels (the legitimate badge/meta content), clean 3-line truncation.

The regenerated fixtures did not catch this because every fixture title is ≤ 51 chars (~3 lines at the lane width), so the >3-line truncation path is never exercised.

Fix — one line:

```css
.title {
  font-size: 12px; flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0;
  /* multi-line, not a one-line ellipsis: long issue titles must wrap
     inside the fixed lane (3-line clamp keeps the cards compact) */
  white-space: normal;
  display: -webkit-box; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; -webkit-line-clamp: 3;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
  overflow: hidden;              /* required for -webkit-line-clamp to clip */
}
```

Then regenerate the fixtures (`bash site/factory/visual-check/capture.sh`) — ideally after adding a long-title card to `fixture.json` (see the fixture-coverage comment)."

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #774._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 6 — `site/factory/styles.css`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-06):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the regenerated fixtures never exercise the clamp/truncation path**

The visual check is the only automated safety net for this CSS, but every title in `visual-check/fixture.json` is ≤ 51 chars — at the ~156px title content width that is at most 3 rendered lines, i.e. exactly at (never past) the `-webkit-line-clamp: 3` limit. The >3-line truncation path — the one this rule exists for — is never rendered by any of the 5 fixtures, which is why the missing `overflow: hidden` (see blocking comment) shipped undetected through "verified live (playwright)".

Real titles do exceed 3 lines: e.g. gh-769's title ("Factory board: scrambled rollups, repeated states, …") is ~160 chars ≈ 6-7 lines at this width.

Suggestion: add one card with a deliberately long title (~150-200 chars) to `fixture.json` and re-run `capture.sh`, so the regenerated fixtures actually pin the truncation behavior.

---

### Thread 7 — `site/factory/styles.css`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-06):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `.lbl` ellipsis is now unreachable; `white-space: normal` is redundant**

Two small polish notes on the same mechanism:

1. With `overflow-wrap: anywhere` added here, a long label now always wraps mid-token instead of overflowing, so `text-overflow: ellipsis` on `.lbl` can never trigger anymore — content always fits by wrapping. That's a fine (arguably better) behavior, but the leftover `text-overflow: ellipsis` is dead code; either drop it or keep it consciously as a fallback for `white-space: nowrap` reintroduction.

2. On `.title` (line 200), `white-space: normal` is the initial value — the old rule's `nowrap` was removed, so this line is a no-op. Harmless if kept as intent documentation.

Optional: the unprefixed standard `line-clamp: 3` (Chrome 130+) could eventually replace the deprecated `-webkit-box` trio; not required for this PR.

---

### Thread 8

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-06):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: One blocking issue — the new 3-line title clamp dropped the `overflow: hidden` that `-webkit-line-clamp` requires to clip, so titles longer than 3 lines render past the clamp and bleed over the badge/meta/stepper rows while a misleading `…` is painted after line 3 (verified by pixel A/B of the rendered board with a >3-line title). One important issue: the regenerated visual-check fixtures contain no title longer than 3 lines, so the truncation path this PR introduces is never exercised by the fixtures.

The `.lane { min-width: 0 }` fix itself is correct and well-commented, and the lane-width/ellipsis goals of #773 are met.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 [styles.css:201](outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md) — add `overflow: hidden` to `.title` (1-line fix)
- ⚠️ [styles.css:202](outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md) — add a >3-line title to `fixture.json` so the clamp path is pinned by the visual check
- 💡 [styles.css:213](outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md) — `.lbl` ellipsis now unreachable; `white-space: normal` on `.title` is a no-op

**Next Steps**:
1. Add `overflow: hidden;` to the `.title` rule
2. Add a long-title fixture card, re-run `bash site/factory/visual-check/capture.sh`, commit refreshed PNGs

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES (re-review, head unchanged)

**Summary**: Re-review of `ai/gh-773` at the same commit (`fd72881e` — diff byte-identical to the previous round, no rework pushed): the one blocking issue from round 1 is still present, so the verdict is unchanged. The 3-line title clamp still lacks the `overflow: hidden` it requires to clip — titles longer than 3 lines are not truncated and bleed over the badge/meta/stepper rows while a misleading `…` is painted after line 3 (verified by pixel A/B of the rendered board).

**Key Issues** (unchanged from round 1, all still open):
- 🚨 [styles.css:201](outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md) — add `overflow: hidden` to `.title` (1-line fix)

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-06):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `-webkit-line-clamp` without `overflow: hidden` does not clip — titles longer than 3 lines bleed over the rows below the title**

`-webkit-line-clamp` only clips content when the element also has `overflow: hidden` (this PR removes the `overflow: hidden` that the old one-line ellipsis rule had). Without it, the box is clamped to 3 lines and an ellipsis is painted after line 3, **but lines 4+ are still painted below the box** (documented on MDN: *"otherwise the content is not clipped, although an ellipsis is still shown"*). On the card that overflow ink lands on the `.labels` / `.meta` / stepper rows.

Verified empirically on this exact board (headless Chromium, `?fixture=` mode, one card patched with a 185-char title — this repo's own PR titles reach that length):

- as shipped (no `overflow: hidden`): **1650** text pixels rendered in the card region below the clamped title box, overlapping the badge/meta/stepper rows, plus a misleading `…` after line 3;

The regenerated fixtures did not catch this because every fixture title is ≤ 51 chars (~3 lines at the lane width), so the >3-line truncation path is never exercised.

Fix — one line:

```css
.title {
  font-size: 12px; flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0;
  /* multi-line, not a one-line ellipsis: long issue titles must wrap
     inside the fixed lane (3-line clamp keeps the cards compact) */
  white-space: normal;
  display: -webkit-box; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; -webkit-line-clamp: 3;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
  overflow: hidden;              /* required for -webkit-line-clamp to clip */
}
```

Then regenerate the fixtures (`bash site/factory/visual-check/capture.sh`) — ideally after adding a long-title card to `fixture.json` (see the fixture-coverage comment).

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.
# This repo's validation CI is `Quality` (display name "Quality") and its
# required context is the `crap` job.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # dmtools-agents#682 (live fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03, still reproducing
  # 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22 in THIS repo — runs 06:36/06:41/06:43): the
  # global group below already ran with cancel-in-progress:false, yet
  # kicker runs kept dying cancelled in chains. cancel-in-progress only
  # shields the RUNNING run — a queued run in the same group ALWAYS
  # supersedes (cancels) the pending one (GitHub docs: "Any existing
  # pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists,
  # will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its
  # place"). One global group meant every push anywhere (silent refresh,
  # factory-data snapshots, dev waves) cancelled every other branch's
  # pending kicker. Per-head-SHA group: no push can displace another
  # push's kicker — a queued kicker that is about to dispatch a tick
  # always gets to run (canonical fix + consumer notes: IstiN/
  # dmtools-agentic-workflows factory-sm-kicker.yml). Effective once the
  # canonical pin is bumped (separate PR): until then the called
  # workflow's own global group still supersedes.
  group: sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: crap

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Regenerate the factory board visual-check fixtures (site/factory/visual-check/).
#
# The board is zero-build and reads live `factory-data` snapshots; these
# fixtures are captured against the BUNDLED fixture snapshot instead
# (visual-check/fixture.json, via the board's ?fixture= mode) so every
# surface — lane summaries, progress bars, backlog lanes, details drawer,
# token table — renders deterministically, no network, no rate limits.
#
# Requires a headless-capable chromium on PATH. The board pins "now" to the
# fixture's tick time in fixture mode, so re-runs produce identical frames.
#
# Usage: bash site/factory/visual-check/capture.sh
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."   # site/factory — the board root (fixture URLs are relative to it)

CHROME="${CHROME:-$(command -v chromium || command -v chromium-browser || command -v google-chrome)}"
BASE="file://$PWD/index.html"
OUT="visual-check"
FIXTURE="visual-check/fixture.json"

shot() { # shot <name> <w> <h> <query>
  local name="$1" w="$2" h="$3" q="$4"
  "$CHROME" --headless=new --no-sandbox --disable-gpu \
    --allow-file-access-from-files --hide-scrollbars \
    --window-size="$w,$h" --virtual-time-budget=5000 \
    --screenshot="$OUT/$name" "$BASE?$q" 2>/dev/null
  echo "  $name"
}

echo "capturing factory-board visual-check fixtures (fixture=$FIXTURE)"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.1440x900.dark.png"          1440 900  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.1440x900.light.png"         1440 900  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=light"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.2048x1320.dark.png"         2048 1320 "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.390x844.dark.mobile.png"    390  844  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark"
# the drawer is an overlay — captured open (deep-linked) as its own frame
shot "factory-board.visual-check.1440x900.dark.drawer.png"   1440 900  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark&drawer=pr-817@validating"
echo "done"

{"command":"node -e \"const f=require('./site/factory/visual-check/fixture.json'); for (const [k,v] of Object.entries(f.lanes)) { for (const c of (Array.isArray(v)?v:[])) { if (c.title) console.log(k, c.pr, c.title.length + ' chars'); } }\""}

      "body": "🚨 **BLOCKING: `-webkit-line-clamp` without `overflow: hidden` does not clip — titles longer than 3 lines bleed over the rows below the title**

`-webkit-line-clamp` only clips content when the element also has `overflow: hidden` (this PR removes the `overflow: hidden` that the old one-line ellipsis rule had). Without it, the box is clamped to 3 lines and an ellipsis is painted after line 3, **but lines 4+ are still painted below the box** (documented on MDN: *"otherwise the content is not clipped, although an ellipsis is still shown"*). On the card that overflow ink lands on the `.labels` / `.meta` / stepper rows.

Verified empirically on this exact board (headless Chromium, `?fixture=` mode, one card patched with a 185-char title — this repo's own PR titles reach that length):

- as shipped (no `overflow: hidden`): **1650** text pixels rendered in the card region below the clamped title box, overlapping the badge/meta/stepper rows, plus a misleading `…` after line 3;
- with `overflow: hidden` added: **210** pixels (the legitimate badge/meta content), clean 3-line truncation.

The regenerated fixtures did not catch this because every fixture title is ≤ 51 chars (~3 lines at the lane width), so the >3-line truncation path is never exercised.

Fix — one line:

```css
.title {
  font-size: 12px; flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0;
  /* multi-line, not a one-line ellipsis: long issue titles must wrap

  white-space: normal;
  display: -webkit-box; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; -webkit-line-clamp: 3;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
  overflow: hidden;              /* required for -webkit-line-clamp to clip */
}
```

Then regenerate the fixtures (`bash site/factory/visual-check/capture.sh`) — ideally after adding a long-title card to `fixture.json` (see the fixture-coverage comment)."

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-06):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `-webkit-line-clamp` without `overflow: hidden` does not clip — titles longer than 3 lines bleed over the rows below the title**

`-webkit-line-clamp` only clips content when the element also has `overflow: hidden` (this PR removes the `overflow: hidden` that the old one-line ellipsis rule had). Without it, the box is clamped to 3 lines and an ellipsis is painted after line 3, **but lines 4+ are still painted below the box** (documented on MDN: *"otherwise the content is not clipped, although an ellipsis is still shown"*). On the card that overflow ink lands on the `.labels` / `.meta` / stepper rows.

Verified empirically on this exact board (headless Chromium, `?fixture=` mode, one card patched with a 185-char title — this repo's own PR titles reach that length):

- as shipped (no `overflow: hidden`): **1650** text pixels rendered in the card region below the clamped title box, overlapping the badge/meta/stepper rows, plus a misleading `…` after line 3;

The regenerated fixtures did not catch this because every fixture title is ≤ 51 chars (~3 lines at the lane width), so the >3-line truncation path is never exercised.

```css
.title {
  font-size: 12px; flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0;
  /* multi-line, not a one-line ellipsis: long issue titles must wrap

  white-space: normal;
  display: -webkit-box; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; -webkit-line-clamp: 3;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
  overflow: hidden;              /* required for -webkit-line-clamp to clip */
}
```

name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # dmtools-agents#682 (live fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03, still reproducing
  # 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22 in THIS repo — runs 06:36/06:41/06:43): the
  # global group below already ran with cancel-in-progress:false, yet
  # kicker runs kept dying cancelled in chains. cancel-in-progress only
  # shields the RUNNING run — a queued run in the same group ALWAYS
  # supersedes (cancels) the pending one (GitHub docs: "Any existing
  # pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists,
  # will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its
  # place"). One global group meant every push anywhere (silent refresh,
  # factory-data snapshots, dev waves) cancelled every other branch's
  # pending kicker. Per-head-SHA group: no push can displace another
  # push's kicker — a queued kicker that is about to dispatch a tick
  # always gets to run (canonical fix + consumer notes: IstiN/
  # dmtools-agentic-workflows factory-sm-kicker.yml). Effective once the
  # canonical pin is bumped (separate PR): until then the called
  # workflow's own global group still supersedes.
  group: sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: crap

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Regenerate the factory board visual-check fixtures (site/factory/visual-check/).
#
# The board is zero-build and reads live `factory-data` snapshots; these
# fixtures are captured against the BUNDLED fixture snapshot instead
# (visual-check/fixture.json, via the board's ?fixture= mode) so every
# surface — lane summaries, progress bars, backlog lanes, details drawer,
# token table — renders deterministically, no network, no rate limits.
#
# Requires a headless-capable chromium on PATH. The board pins "now" to the
# fixture's tick time in fixture mode, so re-runs produce identical frames.
#
# Usage: bash site/factory/visual-check/capture.sh
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."   # site/factory — the board root (fixture URLs are relative to it)

CHROME="${CHROME:-$(command -v chromium || command -v chromium-browser || command -v google-chrome)}"
BASE="file://$PWD/index.html"
OUT="visual-check"
FIXTURE="visual-check/fixture.json"

shot() { # shot <name> <w> <h> <query>
  local name="$1" w="$2" h="$3" q="$4"
  "$CHROME" --headless=new --no-sandbox --disable-gpu \
    --allow-file-access-from-files --hide-scrollbars \
    --window-size="$w,$h" --virtual-time-budget=5000 \
    --screenshot="$OUT/$name" "$BASE?$q" 2>/dev/null
  echo "  $name"
}

echo "capturing factory-board visual-check fixtures (fixture=$FIXTURE)"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.1440x900.dark.png"          1440 900  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.1440x900.light.png"         1440 900  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=light"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.2048x1320.dark.png"         2048 1320 "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.390x844.dark.mobile.png"    390  844  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark"
# the drawer is an overlay — captured open (deep-linked) as its own frame
shot "factory-board.visual-check.1440x900.dark.drawer.png"   1440 900  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark&drawer=pr-817@validating"
echo "done"

{"command":"node -e \"const f=require('./site/factory/visual-check/fixture.json'); for (const [k,v] of Object.entries(f.lanes)) { for (const c of (Array.isArray(v)?v:[])) { if (c.title) console.log(k, c.pr, c.title.length + ' chars'); } }\""}
{"command":"grep -rn \"860\" site/factory/visual-check/fixture.json | head -5; grep -n \"drawer=pr-\" site/factory/visual-check/capture.sh"}

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 6 — `site/factory/styles.css`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-06):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the regenerated fixtures never exercise the clamp/truncation path**

The visual check is the only automated safety net for this CSS, but every title in `visual-check/fixture.json` is ≤ 51 chars — at the ~156px title content width that is at most 3 rendered lines, i.e. exactly at (never past) the `-webkit-line-clamp: 3` limit. The >3-line truncation path — the one this rule exists for — is never rendered by any of the 5 fixtures, which is why the missing `overflow: hidden` (see blocking comment) shipped undetected through "verified live (playwright)".

Real titles do exceed 3 lines: e.g. gh-769's title ("Factory board: scrambled rollups, repeated states, …") is ~160 chars ≈ 6-7 lines at this width.

Suggestion: add one card with a deliberately long title (~150-200 chars) to `fixture.json` and re-run `capture.sh`, so the regenerated fixtures actually pin the truncation behavior.

---

### Thread 7 — `site/factory/styles.css`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-06):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `.lbl` ellipsis is now unreachable; `white-space: normal` is redundant**

Two small polish notes on the same mechanism:

1. With `overflow-wrap: anywhere` added here, a long label now always wraps mid-token instead of overflowing, so `text-overflow: ellipsis` on `.lbl` can never trigger anymore — content always fits by wrapping. That's a fine (arguably better) behavior, but the leftover `text-overflow: ellipsis` is dead code; either drop it or keep it consciously as a fallback for `white-space: nowrap` reintroduction.

2. On `.title` (line 200), `white-space: normal` is the initial value — the old rule's `nowrap` was removed, so this line is a no-op. Harmless if kept as intent documentation.

Optional: the unprefixed standard `line-clamp: 3` (Chrome 130+) could eventually replace the deprecated `-webkit-box` trio; not required for this PR.

---

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: One blocking issue — the new 3-line title clamp dropped the `overflow: hidden` that `-webkit-line-clamp` requires to clip, so titles longer than 3 lines render past the clamp and bleed over the badge/meta/stepper rows while a misleading `…` is painted after line 3 (verified by pixel A/B of the rendered board with a >3-line title). One important issue: the regenerated visual-check fixtures contain no title longer than 3 lines, so the truncation path this PR introduces is never exercised by the fixtures.

The `.lane { min-width: 0 }` fix itself is correct and well-commented, and the lane-width/ellipsis goals of #773 are met.

- 🚨 [styles.css:201](outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md) — add `overflow: hidden` to `.title` (1-line fix)
- ⚠️ [styles.css:202](outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md) — add a >3-line title to `fixture.json` so the clamp path is pinned by the visual check
- 💡 [styles.css:213](outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md) — `.lbl` ellipsis now unreachable; `white-space: normal` on `.title` is a no-op

**Next Steps**:
1. Add `overflow: hidden;` to the `.title` rule
2. Add a long-title fixture card, re-run `bash site/factory/visual-check/capture.sh`, commit refreshed PNGs

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-06):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `-webkit-line-clamp` without `overflow: hidden` does not clip — titles longer than 3 lines bleed over the rows below the title**

`-webkit-line-clamp` only clips content when the element also has `overflow: hidden` (this PR removes the `overflow: hidden` that the old one-line ellipsis rule had). Without it, the box is clamped to 3 lines and an ellipsis is painted after line 3, **but lines 4+ are still painted below the box** (documented on MDN: *"otherwise the content is not clipped, although an ellipsis is still shown"*). On the card that overflow ink lands on the `.labels` / `.meta` / stepper rows.

Verified empirically on this exact board (headless Chromium, `?fixture=` mode, one card patched with a 185-char title — this repo's own PR titles reach that length):

- as shipped (no `overflow: hidden`): **1650** text pixels rendered in the card region below the clamped title box, overlapping the badge/meta/stepper rows, plus a misleading `…` after line 3;
- with `overflow: hidden` added: **210** pixels (the legitimate badge/meta content), clean 3-line truncation.

The regenerated fixtures did not catch this because every fixture title is ≤ 51 chars (~3 lines at the lane width), so the >3-line truncation path is never exercised.

Fix — one line:

```css
.title {
  font-size: 12px; flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0;
  /* multi-line, not a one-line ellipsis: long issue titles must wrap
     inside the fixed lane (3-line clamp keeps the cards compact) */
  white-space: normal;
  display: -webkit-box; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; -webkit-line-clamp: 3;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
  overflow: hidden;              /* required for -webkit-line-clamp to clip */
}
```

Then regenerate the fixtures (`bash site/factory/visual-check/capture.sh`) — ideally after adding a long-title card to `fixture.json` (see the fixture-coverage comment).

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.
# This repo's validation CI is `Quality` (display name "Quality") and its
# required context is the `crap` job.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # dmtools-agents#682 (live fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03, still reproducing
  # 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22 in THIS repo — runs 06:36/06:41/06:43): the
  # global group below already ran with cancel-in-progress:false, yet
  # kicker runs kept dying cancelled in chains. cancel-in-progress only
  # shields the RUNNING run — a queued run in the same group ALWAYS
  # supersedes (cancels) the pending one (GitHub docs: "Any existing
  # pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists,
  # will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its
  # place"). One global group meant every push anywhere (silent refresh,
  # factory-data snapshots, dev waves) cancelled every other branch's
  # pending kicker. Per-head-SHA group: no push can displace another
  # push's kicker — a queued kicker that is about to dispatch a tick
  # always gets to run (canonical fix + consumer notes: IstiN/
  # dmtools-agentic-workflows factory-sm-kicker.yml). Effective once the
  # canonical pin is bumped (separate PR): until then the called
  # workflow's own global group still supersedes.
  group: sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: crap
